title: Crossed products realize every continuous units class
statement: For every field K and every x in its continuous degree-two separable-closure units cohomology [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology], there exists a finite-dimensional central simple K-algebra A with R(A,x), where R is the matrix scalar-defect relation [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect].

source.place: The scalar-defect construction following Lemma 03R6, Theorem 03R7, and Section 0DVG

proof.text: the map from cycles to homology is surjective on underlying modules, since TopModuleCat homology is the algebraic kernel modulo image with quotient topology. Choose a homogeneous cycle representing `x`. Uncurry its iterated continuous maps, using compact Hausdorffness of the Galois group, and evaluate at `(1,g,g*h)` to obtain a continuous multiplicative two-cocycle `c`. Its values have finite image in the discrete units. Compactness and local constancy give an open normal subgroup on whose cosets `c` is constant; shrink it also to fix all values. Its fixed field L is finite Galois over K and `c` is inflated from a cocycle on Gal(L/K) with values in Lˣ. Normalize `c` by a coboundary. Form the crossed product with L-basis `u_g`, multiplication `u_g a = g(a) u_g` and `u_g u_h = c(g,h) u_(g*h)`. The cocycle identity makes this associative and normalization gives its unit. Commuting with L forces a central element into L, and commuting with all `u_g` forces it into K. The usual minimal-support argument proves simplicity, and its K-dimension is `[L:K]^2`. The crossed product splits over L. In its regular splitting representation the projective descent matrices have scalar defect `c` (choose the opposite algebra if the splitting convention gives the inverse class). Inflate those matrices to the absolute Galois group; they are locally constant and satisfy the two equations in `HasBrauerScalarDefect`. Their homogeneous cycle has class `x`, as normalization only changed a coboundary. This supplies the required central simple algebra and realization.
